company.name: Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence

profile_text.body:
The Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence is a nonprofit university lab founded in 2019 and headquartered in Stanford, California. Its site says it advances AI research, education, and policy to improve the human condition, and it describes human-centered AI as an approach that prioritizes human needs, values, and well-being throughout the development and deployment of AI systems. The institute is led by Denning Co-Directors Fei-Fei Li and John Etchemendy. Li's statement on the site frames a human-centered framework for AI research, education, practice, and policy as a historical opportunity and responsibility, and Etchemendy says the field spans the entire university and requires the full range of disciplinary expertise.

The site lists fellowship and grant programs, affinity groups for students, courses for leaders and decision-makers on AI technologies and their business implications, and specialized training for policymakers and civil servants. It also describes work in the K-12 ecosystem with teachers and students. Among the projects named is Clinical Mind AI, described as a Stanford-developed international collaborative platform that uses AI-simulated patient encounters to strengthen clinical reasoning education across health professions. The site reports Stanford research finding that users with limited social networks who seek emotional support from AI companions experience lower well-being, and it cites Erik Brynjolfsson, director of the Stanford Digital Economy Lab and a senior fellow at HAI, arguing that businesses can gain more by using AI to raise employee productivity than by replacing workers. It also notes the Joint California Summit on Generative AI, highlighted in Governor Newsom's Executive Order, and a Stanford Law School effort to build an AI pipeline that combs through millions of local statutes.

The institute's own site presents the AI Index as its comprehensive analysis of AI's trajectory, saying this year's edition shows a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared institutions are to manage it, with governance, evaluation, and understanding falling behind technical capability, investment, and adoption. No products are tracked for the institute, no lawsuits are recorded, and no MCP servers are listed. California is the jurisdiction associated with it, with a count of 270.
